newsitem.title: USA: Hoffmann-La Roche cooperating in Justice probe.
newsitem.headline: Hoffmann-La Roche cooperating in Justice probe.

text.p: Hoffmann-La Roche Inc said Wednesday it has been cooperating in an ongoing U.S. Justice Department investigation of the citric acid industry.

"Our company has been asked by the Justice Department for information and we are providing that requested information and cooperating with the government," Martin Hirsch, a director in Hoffmann-La Roche's public affairs department, said.
Hoffmann-La Roche, based in Nutley, N.J., is a unit of Roche Holding Ltd of Switzerland.
Hirsch declined to comment on whether or not Hoffmann-La Roche is a target of the Justice investigation or if it is involved in negotiations to settle potential charges.
"That I cannot comment on while this is a pending matter," Hirsch said.

Justice officials have said its investigation continues into citric acid, which is used in food, beverages and other products, as well as a probe into high fructose corn syrup, a sweetener. Hoffmann-La Roche does not make high fructose corn syrup.
Archer Daniels Midland Co earlier this week pleaded guilty to two counts of price-fixing in citric acid and lysine, a feed additive. ADM agreed to pay $100 million in fines.
Justice officials said ADM cooperated in the citric acid investigation and has gained immunity to cooperate in the high fructose corn syrup investigation.
